title: From Personal Project to Extended Essay
summary: Personal Project to Extended Essay guidance for MYP Year 5 students, covering transferable skills, key differences, topic choices and next steps.
body_markdown:
The **Personal Project to Extended Essay** transition is not about turning one assignment into a longer version of another. It is about carrying forward the habits you built in MYP Year 5, then adapting them to a more focused academic investigation.


Your MYP Personal Project teaches you to sustain an inquiry, manage a long timeline, evaluate sources, create an outcome and reflect on your decisions. The Extended Essay, completed in the Diploma Programme, asks you to use many of those skills to investigate a focused research question and construct a reasoned academic argument.


The reassuring part is that you are not beginning from zero. You are changing the kind of work those familiar skills must do.


### The transition at a glance


MYP Personal Project Extended Essay


Begins with a personal interest and learning goal Begins with a focused academic research question


Includes a product or outcome Produces a formal piece of academic writing


Emphasizes process, action and reflection Emphasizes research, analysis and argument


Uses product success criteria Uses an academic framework and assessment criteria


Develops approaches to learning skills Requires increasingly independent use of research and communication skills


Completed in the final year of the MYP Completed as part of the DP core


The bridge between them consists of five habits: choosing a meaningful subject, controlling scope, planning independently, handling evidence responsibly and reflecting honestly.


### Meet the student making the transition


Consider a hypothetical MYP Year 5 student named Lina. For her Personal Project, Lina wants to learn how visual design can make recycling instructions easier to understand. Her outcome is a set of illustrated sorting guides for her school.


Under current IB guidance, the MYP Personal Project includes a **process, a product or outcome, and a reflective report** . The wider project follows a cycle of inquiry, action and reflection. Lina therefore needs more than attractive posters. She must define what she wants to learn, plan the work, investigate relevant information, apply skills, evaluate her outcome and explain what the experience changed in her understanding.


That process is excellent preparation for the Extended Essay. But Lina should not assume her future essay will simply be called “Why recycling posters matter.” That is a broad topic, not an analytical research question.


Two students discover that one research question has grown into a jungle of new questions


### What your MYP Personal Project already teaches you


### How to remain interested after the novelty disappears


Long projects are exciting at the beginning. The middle is different. Files become disorganized, an interview is cancelled, or the first design fails. Finishing teaches you that independence is not constant motivation. It is the ability to keep making reasonable decisions when motivation fluctuates.


That lesson matters in the Extended Essay. A topic must be interesting enough to hold your attention, but interest alone cannot carry the investigation. You will need routines, deadlines and a record of your evolving thinking.


### How to turn curiosity into a manageable aim


A student might begin with “I want to explore sustainable fashion.” A manageable Personal Project needs a clearer learning goal and an achievable product. Perhaps the student learns how garment care affects clothing longevity and creates a repair guide for teenagers.


The same narrowing instinct becomes even more important in the DP. RevisionDojo’s guide to[crafting an Extended Essay research question](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-craft-the-perfect-ib-extended-essay-research-question-8-proven-tips) explains how a broad interest must become a precise, researchable problem.


### How to document decisions


Good project records do not merely prove that you worked. They preserve the reasons behind your choices. Record why you rejected a source, changed a criterion, reduced the scope or revised the product.


In an Extended Essay, that habit supports meaningful reflection. “I changed my question” says little. “The available evidence could not support the original comparison, so I limited the investigation to one period” reveals judgment.


### How to evaluate information


A polished webpage is not automatically a reliable source. Your Personal Project gives you an early opportunity to consider authorship, purpose, relevance, evidence and limitations.


The Extended Essay raises the standard. You must select evidence appropriate to the chosen field and acknowledge every borrowed idea correctly. Saving complete citation details while researching is far safer than reconstructing them later.


### What changes in the Extended Essay


The greatest change is the centre of gravity. In the Personal Project, Lina’s learning process and created outcome are central. In the Extended Essay, the investigation is organized around an academic research question, and the final writing must develop a defensible answer.


RevisionDojo’s[MYP Personal Project and Extended Essay comparison](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-vs-extended-essay-key-differences) captures this distinction: the Personal Project demonstrates a learning journey, while the essay develops an academic argument.


### A topic is not yet a research question


“Recycling communication” is a topic. A stronger question identifies what will be examined, where the boundaries lie and what kind of analysis is possible.


Lina’s interest could eventually lead in different directions:


- In visual arts, she might analyse how selected design choices communicate environmental ideas in particular works.
- In psychology, she might investigate a tightly defined question about attention or decision-making using appropriate academic research.
- In an interdisciplinary pathway, she might connect perspectives from two DP subjects where that combination is genuinely necessary.


These are directions, not ready-made questions. The eventual choice must fit the current Extended Essay framework, Lina’s DP subjects, available evidence and her school’s guidance. RevisionDojo’s article on[what makes a research question researchable](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-makes-research-question-researchable) offers a useful feasibility test before a student commits.


### Creation gives way to sustained analysis


A successful product can often be seen or demonstrated. A successful academic argument must be built. It requires claims, evidence, interpretation, counterarguments or limitations where relevant, and a conclusion that answers the question without exaggerating what the evidence proves.


This is why a beautiful MYP outcome does not automatically predict an easy essay. The transferable advantage lies in the planning and inquiry behind the product, not in reusing the product itself.


### How Lina can build a bridge now


Lina does not need to choose her Extended Essay question in MYP Year 5. She can, however, leave the Personal Project with material that will make future research less intimidating.


### Keep a transferable-skills page


At the end of the project, she can create a private one-page record with four headings:


- research decisions that worked
- planning mistakes to avoid
- feedback that changed the work
- questions that remain interesting


This is not an additional IB requirement. It is a practical way to preserve lessons that might otherwise disappear after submission.


### Separate continuation from duplication


A Personal Project may reveal an interest worth pursuing later, but the Extended Essay must be approached as a new academic task. Lina can retain her curiosity about environmental communication without copying her report, recycling assessed material or assuming that her original evidence is sufficient.


The safest principle is simple: continue the **interest** , not the submitted work. When the time comes, she should discuss overlap and academic integrity with her Extended Essay supervisor.


### Practise asking narrower questions


After completing her project, Lina could write three possible questions about its wider theme. She should then test each one:


- Is the question analytical rather than purely descriptive?
- Can it be investigated with accessible, credible evidence?
- Is its scope realistic?
- Does it fit an appropriate academic field?
- Could a conclusion answer it directly?


A research question often improves during investigation. RevisionDojo’s explanation of[why revising the research question matters](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/the-importance-of-research-question-revision-during-the-ee-process) shows that refinement is not failure. It is frequently evidence of better understanding.


### A practical Personal Project to Extended Essay checklist


Before leaving MYP Year 5, ask yourself whether you can:


- explain your learning goal clearly
- show how research influenced your choices
- distinguish strong sources from weak ones
- maintain organized references and project records
- create a realistic plan and revise it when necessary
- evaluate limitations without hiding them
- use supervisor feedback while retaining ownership
- reflect on specific decisions rather than describing events


You do not need to master academic essay writing yet. The aim is to recognize that these habits will return in a more demanding form.


### Using RevisionDojo as the work becomes more academic


The transition becomes easier when each tool has a clear purpose. RevisionDojo’s[Extended Essay guides](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ee-guides) can help students understand subject expectations, research questions, structure and reflection. The Coursework Library can expose students to the shape of strong academic work, while AI Chat can help them interrogate confusing concepts rather than passively collect explanations.


Later, Study Notes and Flashcards can strengthen subject knowledge, and the Questionbank, Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can support the subjects surrounding the core. Grading tools can provide another feedback layer, while RevisionDojo Tutors can help students diagnose uncertainty and plan sensible next steps. None of these replaces the student’s judgment or the official guidance from a school. Their value is in making independent work more deliberate.


### Your project is evidence that you can begin


The MYP Personal Project does not make the Extended Essay effortless. Nothing worthwhile works that way. It gives you something more useful: evidence that you can remain with a question for longer than a lesson, make choices without constant instructions and learn from work that does not unfold exactly as planned.


Lina may never write an Extended Essay about recycling communication. That is not the point. The real bridge is the person she becomes while finishing the project: more careful with evidence, more realistic about time and more willing to revise an idea.


When DP arrives, RevisionDojo can provide the guides, Coursework Library, AI support, study tools, grading feedback and Tutors around that journey. But the first proof of independence will already be there, inside the project she once wondered whether she could finish.
